name: Front-Rack Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A Bulgarian split squat performed with the barbell in the front rack position, resting on the front deltoids. This variation promotes a more upright torso than the back rack version and increases upper back and core stability requirements while heavily loading the working quadriceps and glutes.

execution.starting_position: Position a barbell in the front rack (resting on the clavicles and anterior deltoids). Stand in a split stance with the rear foot elevated on a bench.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the barbell in a rack to shoulder height. Take the front rack position and walk back to position the rear foot on a bench.
steps: Step 1: Brace your core hard and keep elbows high to maintain the front rack position.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee toward the floor by bending both knees.
Step 3: Descend until the front thigh is at or below parallel, keeping the torso upright.
Step 4: Drive through the front heel to return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the descent. Exhale on the ascent.
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows, causing the bar to roll forward off the shoulders
Allowing the front knee to collapse inward
safety_considerations: Front rack requires adequate wrist and shoulder mobility — do not force the position if mobility is limited
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee approaches the floor. Front thigh at or below parallel.
coaching_cues: Drive the front knee out over the pinky toe
